# Issue 168

​​Hello and Happy New Year\! The news didn’t stop for two and a half weeks, even though I (mostly) did, so this note is extra long and will get chopped by your email service. You can just click “issue 168” in the title to scroll through all the links. Fun fact, I think you can do this with most email subscriptions and the admin won’t be able to track your clicks. Or you could just use a dummy, fake email address for your newsletters to be anonymous (I do).  
If you want to read about industry stuff and not personal whereabouts with surfing, skip the three paras below “moving on”. In any event, I want to highlight that Netflix [has a tech blog](https://medium.com/@NetflixTechBlog) that I religiously follow. They recently published an article on how they [use machine learning to support content decision-making](https://netflixtechblog.com/supporting-content-decision-makers-with-machine-learning-995b7b76006f). It’s well worth the read.  
Also, shamelessly signal boosting my first portfolio company: [Hovercast](https://www.hovercast.com/), a groundbreaking interactive live events platform, which found itself in good company with Sundance and New York Comic Con in a just-published article in [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/evolving-events-covid-19/). I want to get them more into streaming theatre, concerts, & festivals… hit me up if you work in those areas (reply directly). They recently produced livestreams with the creators of Hamilton and Elf, and for massive companies like Comcast and Amazon. They’re best in class.  
Moving on…  
I spent the holidays in north New Zealand camping and teaching my friends’ un-disciplined kids how to surf. I grew up at the beach. Lessons learned from surf culture are stitched into my DNA. There is such a thing as surf etiquette. Spicoli and that babbling “so pitted” idiot who went viral a decade ago tarnished our rep. I’ve been smacked and dunked once or twice in my day for not following the code of conduct, which is called ‘a licking’ in Hawaii. My local spot, Salt Creek, was [written about four years ago](https://www.ocregister.com/2017/05/09/clash-in-the-waves-at-salt-creek-ignites-heated-discussion-about-surf-etiquette/) when some kid got splashed. Did he deserve it? Probably, yeah.  
Any who, thought I’d share a few of these guiding ‘principles’ that have pretty much molded me into the person I am today. They seemingly work for the business world as well. Respect \- you’ve got to give it to get it. Style is everything. Be original. Speed, progress, always. Know before you go \- do your diligence. Commit \- go big or go home. Send it for your buddies. Bend at the knees, not the waist \- same applies for the dance floor. Walk the walk \- stickers on a board (or a resume) don’t mean jack. Never brag. Never claim. *Never*. And most importantly, have fun. Be in the moment.  
I’ve written about surfing in [issue 85](https://medium.com/devons-newsletter/issue-85-5-13-19-ed897a503f88) about early Uber investors/execs, [issue 101](https://medium.com/devons-newsletter/issue-101-9-2-19-b20582d9520e) about Surfline (\*Chris Erwin just [published a solid piece](https://www.wearerockwater.com/blog/surfline-gets-30-million) on the Chernin investment), and [issue 123](https://medium.com/devons-newsletter/issue-123-2-10-20-775f6dd04097) about Nike’s Hurley divestiture and when I was sponsored. People always un-sub when I touch on this subject \- that’s fine. This newsletter is just a long con for me to attempt to turn the stereotypical tides. You can scroll through [my Insta](https://www.instagram.com/devonhdolan/) if you want to find some photo evidence that I, uhm, know how to stand up :)  
Back to the task at hand, here are a few industry thoughts and ideas:  
Proof of concepts. There will be a rise of the prototype short film using game engines. I know a few instrumental people at studios that are pushing into this field. So am I. (Hint: check out [Monomyth](https://monomyth.la/)\!) Concept artists have done this for awhile, but they create stunning animated videos that generally don’t tell a story. Like crappy three panel comics. Usually it’s some callback to Ghost in the Shell or Terminator. Come up with your own material. Writing is the best way to brute-force hack your way into Hollywood… second only to being born rich.  
Go indie. Self-publishing and going direct to consumer will seriously grow. Owning your audience has never been more important \- Roku has a huge user base so now they’re going full-stack in success by [bidding on Quibi content](https://www.wsj.com/articles/roku-nears-deal-to-buy-rights-to-quibis-content-11609725389?). There could be other mechanisms, like PVOD windows, that could be offered to core, platinum-level fans. Vimeo, NeuLion, or Shift72 will probably build an off-the-shelf product here. Transact, it’s beautiful.  
Serials. On the written side, novellas can pop up and be released so easily now \- it’s a shame no one hasn’t totally claimed this land. (I think it’s because the masses don’t read that much anyone \- they’re training to be back-up dancers on TikTok) It’s pretty simple to record your voice and distribute them as audiobooks too. Prove your worth, grow your own brand. Wave goodbye to the halcyon days of empire… legacy media.  
Globalization through localization. First, translate your written works for foreign audiences. Hit publish. Then, find a decent text-to-speech program and voila. You are now self-published worldwide in dozens of languages. Hire local editors on the cheap to spruce it up. Distribute everywhere. Audiences lives on networked factions….  
I’m keeping my eyes open for stories that are told through memes and filters that can be *selectively* shared with some incentive-based referral program. Encouraging online word-of-mouth with your closest friends. Socially-networked stories, spaces, that are living and evolving. Messages \-\> community \-\> network \-\> audience.  
To this end, I’ve been thinking about how easy it is to do business and help mint people in today’s age. I literally just forward cool writers and filmmakers on social media to my friends who are reps with a “check this out.” Like twenty years ago you needed a reel and someone to snail mail that out for you. The industry, no longer a walled garden, but its people still hoard information refusing to share it down or up in their organization… like, I know this newsletter is rarely forwarded.  
Locations. Maps. Malls, or portions of them, will morph into entertainment centers not *shopping* centers. They will offer event-driven experiences replete with consumerized, gimmicky, Instagram-able & TikTok-able sideshows. They will be ticketed all-day affairs for the family. There will be movies of course. The other portion of the mall will be used for same-day Amazon fulfillment. Fun\!  
Generative will be the tech buzzword of the year.  
These are all plans, not predictions.  
That’s all for now. Thanks for reading. Here’s to a big year. See you next week.
